gen-dafont-molot-fs-ranade: Heavy, blunt, built like a hammer. Molot's tight c openings and tall lowercase hit hard, while Ranade spreads out in a gentle, slightly stretchy sans-serif; a generous body size would let its wide spacing breathe.
gen-dafont-nasalization-gf-savate: Nasalization floats its letters well apart with no thick-thin pulse at all, and its c opens like calipers. Yet Savate, the sans-serif below, has the sturdier hairlines and a slight pinch where curves meet stems.
gen-dafont-nasalization-mulish: Nasalization's c opens like a pair of calipers. Mulish backs it with a large-x-height sans of uniform stroke and horseshoe-open curves, which makes the pairing feel friendly from top to bottom.
gen-dafont-neogrey-fs-karma: Karma carries the text, a serif whose terminals stop well clear of the stem and whose lowercase nearly meets the caps. Karma keeps a long page smooth, its modulation never snagging the eye beneath Neogrey's lone, geometric letters.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-asap: Glowing and vibrant, Neon draws every letter in one marker-like line. Asap follows in a readable sans with open arc c forms and a low-contrast body height close to the capitals, which carries paragraphs along without tiring.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-be-vietnam-pro: Be Vietnam Pro sets a clean sans with curves that never crowd their endings and strokes like a bent steel rod. And Neon above it glows in stamped-metal lowercase, so a long page of text feels steady underneath.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-erode: Neon-sign glow, fine rope for lines. Erode's tall middle band and shallow ascenders then settle into a dignified rhythm, its gently swelling strokes and wide g and a keeping paragraphs of text easy to travel through.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-fira-sans: Neon lights up the top with tall, stamped-metal lowercase and generous gaps between its letters. It shines at attention; Fira Sans, large in x-height and flat in stroke, does the quiet sans-serif work of reading.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-merriweather-sans: Glowing lines of uniform stout strokes, diagonals as sturdy as uprights. And Merriweather Sans, with tall, large-looking lowercase and an openly turned e, gives the pairing its strongest quality: solid, readable weight at both levels.
gen-dafont-neon-fs-nunito: Nunito brings big, round lowercase bowls and terminals that finish well clear of the stem, a soft sans-serif body. Neon, with its stencil-flat line, is better at glowing; Nunito is better at friendly reading.
